content:
We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1.

Guidance: steps are (in forward direction):
1. Carboxylic acid to amide coupling (forming amide, breaking C-O).
2. Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (forming C=C, breaking C-C and C-O).
3. Sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide.

Thus retrosynthetic steps (reverse) would be:
Step 1 (reverse of amide coupling): break amide bond to give carboxylic acid and amine (the amine is an aniline attached to sulfonyl group? Actually target has amide: C(=O)N attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So reverse: amide -> carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So precursor 1: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (the fragment /C=C/C(=O)N...?). Actually the amide is C(=O)N attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the carboxylic acid precursor would be the α,β-unsaturated acid: /C=C/C(=O)OH attached to the aromatic ring? Wait the target: .../C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. So the amide carbonyl attached to N of aniline. The α,β-unsaturated acid precursor would be /C=C/C(=O)OH attached to the aromatic ring (the same phenyl ring c2ccc(... )cc2). So we need that acid.

Step 2 (reverse of Doebner): break the α,β-unsaturated acid into aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification forms α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. So reverse: α,β-unsaturated acid -> aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid (or maybe malonic acid decarboxylates to give the double bond). So we need aromatic aldehyde precursor: the aromatic ring c2ccc(??)cc2 with aldehyde at position where the side chain attaches. The side chain is attached via a double bond to the aromatic ring. So the aldehyde would be something like c2ccc(CHO)cc2 (para to sulfonyl group). So precursor: p-CHO phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Wait sulfonyl part is attached to the first phenyl ring (c1ccc(NS(=O)(=O) ... )cc1). The second phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) is attached to sulfonyl group and has the side chain. So the aldehyde would be on that second phenyl ring.

Step 3 (reverse of sulfonamide formation): break sulfonamide bond to give sulfonyl chloride and amine (the first phenyl ring with an amine). So precursor: aniline (p-toluidine) with sulfonyl chloride attached? Actually target has NS(=O)(=O) attached to first phenyl ring (p-tolyl). So reverse: the sulfonamide bond cleavage gives p-toluidine (aniline with methyl) and sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl ring (p-sulfonyl chloride). So precursor: p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) and p-sulfonyl chloride phenyl (the second phenyl ring with sulfonyl chloride). But the second phenyl also later gets the side chain via Doebner and amide steps. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor is the aromatic ring bearing sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) and later will be functionalized to have the side chain.

Thus overall retrosynthesis:

Target -> (1) break amide: gives α,β-unsaturated acid (Ar-CH=CH-COOH) attached to second phenyl ring, plus aniline (c3ccccc3N) (which is an aniline attached to the amide nitrogen). Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So the amine fragment is an aniline with an extra NH2? Wait Nc3ccccc3N means the amide nitrogen attached to an aniline that also has an NH2 substituent? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline where the nitrogen is attached to the aromatic ring at position 1, and there is another N at the other end? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline with an amino group at the opposite position? It is a phenyl with two amino substituents: one attached to the amide (as N-aryl) and another free NH2 at the other end. So the amine fragment is 1,4-diaminobenzene? Actually the SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline where the N is attached to the aromatic carbon (position 1) and there is another N attached to the aromatic carbon at position? The SMILES "Nc3ccccc3N" means N attached to aromatic carbon (position 1) and the aromatic ring has another N attached at the end (position 6). So it's p-phenylenediamine (1,4-diaminobenzene). So the amine fragment is p-phenylenediamine.

Thus step 1: amide cleavage gives α,β-unsaturated acid attached to second phenyl, and p-phenylenediamine.

Step 2: α,β-unsaturated acid -> aromatic aldehyde (p-formyl phenyl sulfonyl?) + malonic acid. So aldehyde precursor is p-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached later, but at this stage we have the aromatic ring with sulfonyl group? The sulfonyl group is attached to the first phenyl ring, not the second. Wait the sulfonamide is between the first phenyl (with methyl) and the sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl. The sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be that second phenyl ring bearing sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl). The aldehyde precursor would be that same aromatic ring bearing an aldehyde (Ar-CHO). So we need a transformation that converts Ar-CHO to Ar-CH=CH-COOH via Doebner with malonic acid. So the aldehyde is attached to the second phenyl ring, which also later will be sulfonylated? Actually sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl ring, not the first. Wait the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O)c2... So the sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl ring, and the nitrogen of the sulfonamide is attached to the first phenyl ring (p-toluidine). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor is the second phenyl ring with sulfonyl chloride substituent (Ar-SO2Cl). The aldehyde is also on that same ring (para to the sulfonyl chloride?). In target, the side chain attaches at para position relative to sulfonyl group? The SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonyl group attaches to the second phenyl at position 1, and the side chain attaches at position 4 (para). So the aldehyde precursor would be p-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride (4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride). Good.

Step 3: sulfonamide formation reverse: break sulfonamide to give p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) and p-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride.

Thus we have three steps.

Now we need to find template IDs for each transformation. We have some templates from earlier search results. For amide coupling reverse (i.e., amide formation forward), we need a template that forms amide from acid and amine. The search result with reaction_id 401931 seems to be amide formation with double bond? Actually its retro_smarts_template: '[#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])/[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]>>C-C(-C)(-C)-O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[#7:2])=[O;D1;H0:3].O-C(=O)-[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]'. This is reverse of amide formation with α,β-unsaturated acid? It shows amide with double bond to acid. That matches our amide step (amide attached to α,β-unsaturated acid). So template_id likely 401931? Actually the result includes reaction_id and template_hash. The tool expects template_id (string). Probably we can use reaction_id as template_id? The spec says template_id is a string identifier. We'll assume using reaction_id as string.

Similarly, Doebner modification template: need a template that forms α,β-unsaturated acid from aldehyde + malonic acid. Search maybe not found. Could use template 659569? That is sulfonyl chloride? Not sure. Let's search for functional groups broken: aldehydes, formed: C-C double bonds, carboxylic acid. Use functional_groups_broken ["aldehydes"], functional_groups_formed ["C-C double bonds", "aliphatic carboxylic acid"].
